chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat who said, 'Informed me some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said,'

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ibn Muslim, the people are people of show-off, apart from you, and that is because you have concealed what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves, and displayed what the people love, while the people have displayed what angers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and concealed what Allah loves. O Ibn Muslim, indeed Allah, Blessed and High, was merciful to you, so He made Mut'ah a substitute for you instead of the drinks.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Mut'ah as a substitute for drinks in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) contrasts the general public, who display what angers God and conceal what pleases Him, with the Shia, who conceal their good deeds and display what people love. This distinction highlights the Shia virtue of *khufya* (concealment) in worship, ensuring sincerity (*ikhlas*) is not compromised by the desire for human praise. As a divine mercy to manage human desires, God permitted *Mut'ah* (temporary marriage) as a lawful substitute for intoxicating drinks, offering a practical outlet for physical needs within the community.

en.hubeali: H 14581 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Asbaat who said, ‘Informed me, some of our companions, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said:

Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘O Ibn Muslim, the people are show-offs apart from you, and that is what you have concealed what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Loves, and have displayed what the people love, whilst the people have displayed what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Angered by, and concealed what Allahazwj Loves. O Ibn Muslim, Allahazwj Blessed and High Sympathised with you, so Heazwj Made the Mut’a (Temporary marriage) (Permissible) instead of the (intoxicating) drinks’.
